Recognizance

rih-KOG-nih-zunss · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Recognizance is a formal promise made to a court, often to appear at a future date.

Out of an abundance of caution, the magistrate still required a small bond even after accepting the young man's recognizance.

Worked Example

The visiting student, arrested for a minor traffic violation, was freed on recognizance after promising in writing to appear at his court date before flying home.

A recognizance is essentially a formal, on-the-record promise to the court -- no money changes hands, but breaking it has serious consequences.

How Recognizance Sits Among Its Neighbors

pledge

Antonyms

forfeiture

forfeiture: the loss of something as a penalty for failing to comply

noncompliance

noncompliance: failure to act as required or promised

How Strong Is It? — promise → recognizance → bond

promise vs. recognizance

promise vs. recognizance: A general promise is a casual, spoken commitment with no legal weight behind it.

bond vs. recognizance

bond vs. recognizance: A bond is an actual, money-backed guarantee -- a stronger, more formal commitment than a plain recognizance.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — re-

prefix — re-: again, intensively (Latin)

root — cognoscere

root — cognoscere: to know (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Recognizance comes from re- + Latin cognoscere ('to know') -- it's built the same way as the word recognize, and originally meant a formally acknowledged, on-the-record promise.

Use the root in a new word: incognito

Use the root in a new word: incognito: The movie star traveled incognito, wearing a plain hat and sunglasses so no one would recognize her.
